title: Support of a finite type quasi-coherent module: closed, and proper over the base iff the module lives on a closed subscheme proper over the base
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. (1) The support $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] is a closed subset of $X$. (2) $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] if and only if there is a closed subscheme $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], such that $Z\to S$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F=0$ (that is, $as=0$ for all local sections $a$ of $\mathcal I_Z$ and $s$ of $\mathcal F$ over a common open; equivalently $\mathcal F=i_*\mathcal G$ for a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$). One may take for $Z$ the scheme-theoretic support of $\mathcal F$, the closed subscheme cut out by the annihilator ideal sheaf of $\mathcal F$, whose underlying set is $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYS (lemma-module-support-proper-over-base), (1)<=>(2)<=>(3), with Morphisms Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type, literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex) for closedness of the support and Morphisms Definition 05JV / Lemma 05JU (scheme-theoretic support)

proof.text: (Part (1): the support is closed.) $\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type on the scheme $X$, so $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is a closed subset of $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] (on each affine open $U$ it is $V(\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}(\mathcal F(U)))$). In particular the condition `$\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is proper over $S$' of [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](1) makes sense.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, paragraph before Lemma 0CYS and first sentence of its proof, citing Morphisms Lemma 056J (morphisms-lemma-support-finite-type)

proof.text: (The scheme-theoretic support.) Let $i_F:Z_F\to X$ be the scheme-theoretic support of $\mathcal F$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support]: a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is the annihilator ideal sheaf $\operatorname{Ann}(\mathcal F)$, with $i_F(Z_F)=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support](3) and $\operatorname{Ann}(\mathcal F)\,\mathcal F=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support](4). So $Z_F$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ whose underlying closed subset is $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ and whose ideal sheaf kills $\mathcal F$; this is the last sentence of the statement.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 05JU (morphisms-lemma-scheme-theoretic-support) and Definition 05JV (morphisms-definition-scheme-theoretic-support); used in the proof of Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 0CYS ((1)<=>(2): the scheme theoretic support has underlying closed subset Supp(F))

proof.text: (Part (2), `only if'.) Assume $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is proper over $S$. The closed subscheme $Z_F$ of step 2 is a closed subscheme structure on the closed subset $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, so $Z_F\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](1) (`proper over $S$' implies properness for every closed subscheme structure). With $Z=Z_F$ and $\mathcal I_Z=\operatorname{Ann}(\mathcal F)$ we have $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F=0$ (step 2), which is the required closed subscheme; in particular one may take for $Z$ the scheme-theoretic support.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYS, (1)=>(2) via Definition 0CYM (definition-proper-over-base) and Lemma 0CYL (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), and (2)=>(3)

proof.text: For the reverse implication take the given finite type quasi-coherent G and isomorphism F ≅ i_*G. Let D be the closed range of i, and C the closed support from step 1. At a point outside D, the pushforward stalk is subsingleton by lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks (1). The composite of the forgetful functor, the abelian presheaf functor and the stalk functor maps the given module isomorphism to an isomorphism of abelian groups. Its hom is injective, so the stalk of F is also subsingleton. This proves C ⊆ D. Properness of i followed by f makes D proper over S by lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties (1), and its part (2) then makes C proper over S. The supplied pushforward isomorphism thus replaces the sectionwise complementary-open annihilation calculation.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 0CYS, implication (3) => (1), with Sheaves Lemma 00AE for vanishing of pushforward stalks off a closed image

proof.text: For the scheme-theoretic support immersion i from step 2, use hker to express its sectionwise annihilation as membership in i.ker.idealOfOpens. Apply part (2) of lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated: the explicitly constructed module G = (tensorPullback i).obj F is quasi-coherent and finite type, and the fixed canonical adjunction unit is invertible. Its asIso yields F ≅ i_*G. This supplies the pushforward witness both for the forward direction of the characterization and for the final conjunct. The reverse direction uses the pushforward isomorphism supplied in its hypothesis, as in step 4; it does not use part (1) of the annihilation theorem.

lean.statement: theorem module_support_proper_over_base {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] : (∃ Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X, (Z : Set X) = {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)}) ∧ (HasSupportProperOver f F ↔ ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i), IsProper (i ≫ f) ∧ (∀ (V : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, V)), a ∈ i.ker.idealOfOpens V → ∀ s : Γ(F, V), a • s = 0) ∧ ∃ (G : Z.Modules) (_ : G.IsQuasicoherent) (_ : G.IsFiniteType), Nonempty (F ≅ (pushforward i).obj G)) ∧ (∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i), (∀ U : X.affineOpens, i.ker.ideal U = Module.annihilator Γ(X, U) Γ(F, U)) ∧ Set.range i = {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} ∧ (∀ (V : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, V)), a ∈ i.ker.idealOfOpens V → ∀ s : Γ(F, V), a • s = 0) ∧ (∃ (G : Z.Modules) (_ : G.IsQuasicoherent) (_ : G.IsFiniteType), Nonempty (F ≅ (pushforward i).obj G)) ∧ (HasSupportProperOver f F ↔ IsProper (i ≫ f)))
